title: RSV (Respiratory Syncytial Virus) Vaccine
overview: RSV vaccine can prevent disease caused by infection with Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV).

sections.RSV disease refers to an infection of th: with chronic heart or lung diseaseswith weakened immune systemsnursing home or long-term care facility residentsRSV is usually spread through direct contact with the virus such as droplets from another person's cough or sneeze contacting your eyes, nose or mouth. It can also be spread by touching a surface that has a virus on it, such as a doorknob, and then touching your face before washing your hands.
sections.Mild symptoms of RSV disease typically r: runny nosedecrease in appetitecoughingsneezingfeverwheezingIn individuals at high risk of serious disease as previously described, RSV may cause shortness of breath and low oxygen levels or may also worsen chronic heart or lung disease, leading to a hospital stay and even potentially death.

People who are moderately or severely ill should usually wait until they recover before getting RSV vaccine.Your health care provider can give you more information.
sections.Side effects that have been reported wit:
Redness, swelling, pain, or tenderness where the shot is givenfeverfeeling tiredheadachenauseadiarrheamuscle or joint painSerious neurologic reactions, including Guillan-Barre Syndrome (GBS), have been reported very rarely after RSV vaccine in clinical trials.
In a study of adults 65 years of age and older an association between vaccination with RSV vaccine and development of GBS within 42 days was reported.
Tell your provider if you have sudden weakness, tingling in the hands or feet, or pain.People sometimes faint after medical procedures, including vaccination. Tell your provider if you feel dizzy or have vision changes or ringing in the ears.As with any medicine, there is a very remote chance of a vaccine causing a severe allergic reaction, other serious injury, or death.
